cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Dancing is something that humans do when they want to have a good time.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: It's a universal response to music, found in all cultures.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: But what's only been discovered recently is that dancing not only makes us feel good,

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: it's also extremely good for our health.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Dancing, like other forms of exercise, releases hormones, such as dopamine, which make us

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: feel relaxed and happy. And it also reduces feelings of stress or anxiety.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Dancing is also a sociable activity, which is another reason it makes us feel good.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: One study compared people's enjoyment of dancing at home in front of a video with dancing

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: in a group in a studio.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: The people dancing in a group reported feeling happier, whereas those dancing alone did

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: not.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: In another experiment, university researchers at York and Sheffield took a group of

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: students and sent each of them into a lab where music was played for five minutes.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Each had to choose from three options: to sit and listen quietly to the music, to cycle

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: on an exercise bike while they listened, or to get up and dance.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: All were given cognitive tasks to perform before and after.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: The result showed that those who chose to dance showed much more creativity when doing

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: problem-solving tasks.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Doctor Lovatt at the University of Hertfordshire believes dance could be a very useful

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: way to help people suffering from mental health problems.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: He thinks dance should be prescribed ad therapy to help people overcome issues such as

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: depression.
